fast.why: Today is Wednesday, 1 Jamadilakhir. Tomorrow is a Thursday: deeds are presented to Allah on Mondays and Thursdays, and the Prophet ﷺ liked to be fasting when his deeds were presented. Make your niyyah tonight.

blessing: Your ability to stand up and do your duty today. Strength and a working body are daily gifts. Say Alhamdulillah when you wake, and thank one colleague by name today.

verse.text: Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.

hadith.text: Whoever seeks to be patient, Allah will make him patient. And no one has been given a gift better and more vast than patience.

lesson.title: Taharah and fasting (Shafi'i): the niyyah of the fast
lesson.text: In the Shafi'i school, a fast is not valid without niyyah (intention) in the heart. For an obligatory fast such as Ramadan, the niyyah must be made at night, before Fajr (Sunan Abi Dawud 2454). For a sunnah fast such as tomorrow's Thursday, you may make the niyyah in the morning as long as you have not eaten or drunk since Fajr and it is before the sun passes its zenith (Sahih Muslim 1154). Saying it aloud is recommended to help the heart, but the intention itself is in the heart.

quote.text: Don't have sleepless nights over your enemies. The Almighty will take care of them and give them their due for causing all the hurt. Have faith things will work out and that you'll emerge better than you were before.

name.text: He rewards even small deeds many times over. "Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative" (35:34). Every prayer and every quiet effort at work is seen. Thank Him, knowing He thanks you first.
He brings ease from places we do not see. "Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?" (67:14). Tonight, trust that He is arranging things gently, even on a tiring day.

quote.text: Almighty. Grant us hearts filled with gratitude. May we count our blessings instead of our problems. We ask You for strength in times of need, peace in chaos, joy in sadness and hope in hopelessness. We know You won't disappoint. Aameen.

world.text: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set it at 85 seconds to midnight on 27 Jan 2026, the closest ever, citing nuclear risk, AI and great-power rivalry.
Forecasters' chance of a 'World War Three' before 2050 (10M+ deaths, major powers involved).
Prof Jiang's latest lectures on geopolitics and where great-power conflict is heading.

Nuclear deterrence makes all-out war a losing move for every major power, so the stable outcome (flashing) is 'compete, don't fight': trade wars, arms races and proxy conflicts. The real danger is a misread in a crisis like Taiwan or Ukraine, which is why the clock and the forecast are rising. Meter: 2 of 5.
